title: Quota + Auth liveness handoff brief
content:
Sync summary

Purpose: quick, actionable handoff for the week of 2026-04-12 focused on quota blowups, auth token churn, and liveness flakiness observed in routing. This is not an incident postmortem — just a standup-to-handoff note so on-call and next-shift engineers have context.

Attendees (standup snapshot):
- Maya (owner) — platform, control plane routing
- Liam — allocator + routing fallthroughs
- Sofia — auth & identity
- Ethan — quotas & rate-limiter
- Diego (joined late) — SRE quick consult

Topline observables (what we saw last 48h):
- Two customer-facing throttles where quota enforcement returned 429s incorrectly after a scaling event (high correlation with pod churn). Spike timestamps: 2026-04-11 02:13 UTC and 2026-04-11 19:07 UTC.
- Auth service rotated ephemeral keys during a KMS rotation window; ~0.4% of tokens failed validation for ~7m. Token refresh flow was retried but caused visible latency for some requests.
- Liveness probe flapping on a small subset of controlplane replicas after rolling update — readiness vs liveness mismatch due to cache warm-up (KV cache priming).

Immediate hypotheses (quick, testable):
1) Quota metadata race: when new pods join /leave, the quota shard reconciler is lagging and sometimes double-applies backfills that temporarily re-enable quotas incorrectly. (PLAT-8812)
2) KMS rotation ordering: auth service did rotation of verification keys before propagation to all verification caches — small window where tokens signed with old key still validated by some nodes but not others. Need to change rotation handshake. (PLAT-8846)
3) Liveness/readiness probe ordering: readiness requires KV cache primed, liveness only checks process heartbeat — during rolling update some pods pop as ready before cache is populated, then fail liveness checks under load.

What we tried during standup (quick mitigations):
- Rolled quota reconciler back to prior version (rollback PR linked) to stop further incorrect 429s. Temporary mitigations: increased grace window for quota shard handover to 90s.
- Added an ephemeral feature-flag to auth to opt into staged key swap (feature-flag off now) while we prepare handshake.
- Bumped liveness probe thresholds for the canary pool to give cache warm up 30s. Monitoring for regressions.

Action items (owner, ETA):
- Ethan: deep-dive on quota handover ordering + small repro harness to simulate shard rebalancing during scale events. Deliverable: repro and proposed fix by 2026-04-16. (JIRA PLAT-8812)
- Sofia: draft a KMS rotation handshake spec — two-phase commit for verification cache invalidation + propagation checks. Spec due 2026-04-15; prototype handshake library 2026-04-22. (JIRA PLAT-8846)
- Liam: add extra metrics and tracing spans around quota reconciler transitions (start/finish events, decision reasons) and deploy to staging by 2026-04-14.
- Maya: coordinate on-call handover note + update runbook with temporary grace windows; add checklist for rolling updates that touch KV cache services by 2026-04-13 EOD.
- Diego: SRE to review canary probe bump and give go/no-go for production widening by 2026-04-14.

Short-term priorities (ranking):
1) Stop customer 429 regressions (Ethan + Liam)
2) Fix KMS rotation ordering to remove user-visible latency (Sofia)
3) Stabilize liveness/readiness during rolling updates (Liam + Diego)
4) Improve telemetry for faster RCA (cross-team)

Notes-to-self / gotchas we flagged: 
- When testing quota fixes locally, remember that the allocator stub uses a deterministic seed — it will hide some races we only see with real pod churn. Use the chaos-harness script (tools/chaos/allocator-rebalance) in staging.
- Auth token TTLs currently overlap with rotation window; consider shortening TTL or moving to a single ephemeral signing key with key-wrap for distribution if handshake will take >1min.
- Metrics to monitor after changes: quota.reconcile.latency, quota.enforcement.errors, auth.key.propagation.ms (new), probe.cache.warmup.ms, controlplane.request.retry_rate.

Open questions / discussion items for next sync:
- Should we move toward a centralized quota service that holds authoritative state instead of per-shard reconciler? Tradeoffs: simpler consistency vs single-op throughput risk. (Longer-term)
- Do we want to standardize rotation handshake across services (auth, signer, telemetry)? If yes, start a cross-team RFC.
- How aggressive should our automatic fallthrough be for quotas during scale events? Current policy briefly allows requests to pass if backend is unavailable for <60s — is that acceptable?

Handoff checklist for next shift (bullet actions):
- Confirm rollout rollback is holding and no new 429 clusters in last 3hr window. (Ethan)
- Check auth service error-rate for token validation 5xx/4xx spikes. (Sofia)
- Watch staging for quota reconciler new metrics after Liam's deploy. Look for prolonged reconcile durations >5s.
- If liveness flaps recur, revert probe bump and scale up canary by +2 replicas. (Diego)

Logs & quick links: 
- Incident thread (internal): https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0PLATFORM/p1651201234567
- Repro harness (staging): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/tree/main/tools/chaos/allocator-rebalance
- Quota rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3138
- KMS rotation notes (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PLAT/KMS+rotation+handshake+notes (draft)

Final quick thoughts: keep fixes minimal and observable — our highest risk is churning too many knobs at once and making RCA harder. Prioritize a single small change per area with clear dashboards and alert thresholds.

-- end of brief --
